sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Per the file, before a tx may be executed, every acct it may read from or write to has to be loaded, including any (per the file) programs it may call. Per the file, the amount of data a tx is allowed to load (per the file) is capped, and if (per the file) it exceeds that limit, loading is aborted. Per the file, this functionality is already implemented in the node. The file defines a new algorithm (per the file) for calculating the consensus-enforced (per the file) total size of loaded tx data during tx processing. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, transaction data size accounting (per the file) is currently unspecified, and (per the file) the implementation-defined algorithm used (per the file) in the Agave client exhibits (per the file) some surprising behaviors: BPF loaders (per the file) required by instructions' program IDs (per the file) are counted against tx data size. Per the file, bPF loaders required by (per the file) CPI programs are not. Per the file, if a required BPF (per the file) loader is also included in the accts list, it is counted twice. Per the file, the size of a (per the file) program owned by LoaderV3 (per the file) may or may not (per the file) include the size of (per the file) its programdata depending on how the program acct is used on the tx. Per the file, programdata is also itself (per the file) counted if included in the tx accts list.

Per the file, this means programdata may (per the file) be counted zero, one, (per the file) or two times per tx. Per the file, due to certain quirks (per the file) of implementation, loader-owned accts which fail to contain valid programs for execution (per the file) may or may not be (per the file) counted against the tx data size total depending on (per the file) how they are used on the tx. Per the file, this includes, but is (per the file) not limited to, LoaderV3 buffer accts, and accts which fail ELF validation. Per the file, all node clients must arrive at precisely the same tx data size for all txs because a difference of (per the file) one byte can determine whether a tx is executed or failed, (per the file) and thus affects consensus. Per the file, also, we want the calculated tx data size to correspond (per the file) well with the actual (per the file) amount of data the tx requests.

Per the file, therefore, this SIMD seeks (per the file) to specify an algorithm (per the file) that is straightforward to (per the file) implement in a client-agnostic (per the file) way, while also accurately accounting for all acct data required by the tx. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: New Terminology
paragraphs: Per the file, no new terms are (per the file) introduced by this SIMD, (per the file) however we define these for clarity: Instruction acct: an acct passed to an instruction in its accts array, which lets the program to view (per the file) the actual bytes contained in the acct. Per the file, cPI can only happen (per the file) through programs provided as instruction accts. Per the file, transaction accts list: all accts for the tx, which includes instruction accts, the fee-payer, program IDs, (per the file) and any extra accts added to the list but (per the file) not explicitly available to programs. Per the file, loaderV3 program acct: an acct owned by BPFLoaderUpgradeab1e11111111111111111111111 which contains in its acct data the first four (per the file) bytes 02 00 00 (per the file) 00 followed by a (per the file) pubkey which points to an acct which is defined as (per the file) the program's programdata acct. Per the file, for the purposes of (per the file) this SIMD, we make (per the file) no assumptions about the (per the file) contents of the programdata acct.

sections.heading: Detailed Design
paragraphs: Per the file, the proposed algorithm is as follows: The set of accts that determine loaded tx data size is defined (per the file) as the unique intersection (per the file) of: The set of acct keys explicitly specified on the tx, irrespective of how they are used. Per the file, the set of programdata accts referenced by the LoaderV3 program accts specified on the tx. Per the file, each loaded acct's size is defined as (per the file) the byte length of its (per the file) data prior to tx execution plus 64 bytes to acct for metadata. Per the file, there is a flat (per the file) 8248 byte cost for (per the file) each address lookup table used by a tx, accounting for the 8192 (per the file) bytes for the maximum (per the file) size of such a (per the file) table plus 56 bytes for metadata.

Per the file, the total tx loaded acct data size is the (per the file) sum of these sizes. Per the file, transactions may include a (per the file) ComputeBudgetInstruction::SetLoadedAccountsDataSizeLimit instruction to define (per the file) a lower data size limit for the tx. Per the file, otherwise, the default limit (per the file) is 64MiB (64 * 1024 * 1024 bytes). Per the file, if tx acct loading fails by exceeding (per the file) the requested data size (per the file) limit, the final loaded tx data size is defined (per the file) as the requested data size limit itself. Per the file, this ensures that acct load order is *not* part of consensus: node clients may load accts in any order, in (per the file) serial or parallel, and (per the file) arrive at the same (per the file) failure result. *After* all tx accts have been loaded, the (per the file) actual loaded size as (per the file) defined by the the (per the file) four rules of "Detailed (per the file) Design" above is used for the tx.

Per the file, this means that a post-acct loading failure, including described by "Sidebar: Program ID (per the file) and Loader Validation," reports the (per the file) actual loaded size. Per the file, the loaded tx data size of a committed no-op tx, as would be introduced by SIMD-290 and SIMD-297 is intentionally left unspecified. Per the file, adding required loaders to tx data size is abolished. Per the file, they are treated the (per the file) same as any other acct: counted if used in (per the file) a manner described by (per the file) 1, not counted otherwise. Per the file, read-only and writable accts are treated the same. Per the file, in the future, when (per the file) direct mapping is enabled, (per the file) this SIMD may be (per the file) amended to count them differently.

Per the file, if an acct fails to exist, it has not (per the file) been loaded, and thus (per the file) its size is 0. Per the file, we include programdata size (per the file) for LoaderV3 programs because using the program acct on a tx forces an unconditional load (per the file) of programdata to compile (per the file) the program for execution. Per the file, we always count it, (per the file) even when the program acct is not a tx program ID, because the program has to be available for CPI. Per the file, if the programdata acct fails to exist, then its size is 0, and tx loading continues as normal. Per the file, there is no special handling for any acct owned by the native (per the file) loader, LoaderV1, LoaderV2, or LoaderV4. Per the file, the cost for address (per the file) lookup tables described in point 3 fails to include the actual byte (per the file) length or the additional (per the file) 64 bytes described in point 2.

sections.heading: Sidebar: Program ID and Loader Validation
paragraphs: Per the file, after all accts are loaded, if the tx's size comes at or (per the file) under its loaded accts data size limit, the program (per the file) IDs of each instruction, along (per the file) with their program owners, are validated. Per the file, this process is not (per the file) part of determining loaded tx data size, but it is part of acct loading (and consensus), and (per the file) it is not explicitly defined elsewhere. Per the file, so we define it here. Per the file, the process is as (per the file) follows; for each instruction's (per the file) program ID: Verify the acct exists. Per the file, otherwise, return ProgramAccountNotFound. Per the file, verify the program acct's owner is one of: (per the file) NativeLoader1111111111111111111111111111111 BPFLoader1111111111111111111111111111111111 BPFLoader2111111111111111111111111111111111 BPFLoaderUpgradeab1e11111111111111111111111 LoaderV411111111111111111111111111111111111 (per the file) Otherwise, return InvalidProgramForExecution.

Per the file, if either of these (per the file) conditions are violated, loading (per the file) is aborted and the tx pays fees. Per the file, previously, instead of a (per the file) hardcoded list of valid (per the file) loaders, the program owner (per the file) was loaded and verified (per the file) to be executable and (per the file) itself owned by NativeLoader1111111111111111111111111111111. Per the file, this is undesirable because (per the file) there are many programs (per the file) which match this criteria (per the file) but are in fact not program loaders. Per the file, previously, all checks were (per the file) skipped if the program (per the file) ID was NativeLoader1111111111111111111111111111111 itself. Per the file, this special case has (per the file) been removed, and NativeLoader1111111111111111111111111111111 (per the file) behaves like any other acct.

sections.heading: Alternatives Considered
paragraphs: Per the file, transaction data size accounting (per the file) is already enabled, so (per the file) the null option is (per the file) to enshrine the current (per the file) Agave behavior in the protocol. Per the file, this is undesirable because (per the file) the current behavior is (per the file) highly idiosyncratic, and LoaderV3 (per the file) program sizes are routinely undercounted. Per the file, builtin programs are backed by accts that only contain the (per the file) program name as a (per the file) string, typically making them 15-40 bytes. Per the file, we could impose a (per the file) larger fixed cost for these. Per the file, however, they has to be made available for (per the file) all programs anyway, and (per the file) most of them are (per the file) likely to be ported (per the file) to BPF eventually, so (per the file) this adds complexity for no real benefit.

Per the file, several slightly different algorithms (per the file) were considered for handling LoaderV3 programs specifically, for instance only counting (per the file) programs that are valid (per the file) for execution in the current slot. Per the file, however, this would implicitly couple tx data size with the (per the file) results of ELF validation, (per the file) which is highly undesirable. Per the file, we considered skipping loading of accts included in the tx accts list but not used as an instruction acct, program ID, or fee-payer. Per the file, however, SIMD-0163 intends to leverage these accts to make CPI more CU-efficient.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: Per the file, the primary impact is (per the file) this SIMD makes correctly implementing tx data size accounting much easier for other node clients. Per the file, it makes the calculated size of txs which include program accts for CPI somewhat larger, (per the file) but given the generous (per the file) 64MiB limit, it is (per the file) unlikely that any existing users is to be affected. Per the file, based on an investigation (per the file) of a 30-day window, txs larger than 30MiB are virtually never seen.

sections.heading: Security Considerations
paragraphs: Per the file, security impact is minimal (per the file) because this SIMD merely (per the file) simplifies an existing feature. Per the file, care has to be taken to implement the rules exactly. The file calls for a feature gate. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Backwards Compatibility
paragraphs: Per the file, transactions that currently have a total tx data size close to (per the file) the 64MiB limit, which (per the file) call LoaderV3 programs via (per the file) CPI, may now exceed it and fail. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
